name: Beefeater
label: Dischord
lede: Two years, two LPs, a vegetarian singer fronting a band called Beefeater, and a guitarist who taught DC punk to swing.

eras.title: A Swiss kid, a slap bass, a vegetarian's band
eras.text: Tomas Squip came to Washington from Switzerland around 1981 and drummed in Red C before he ever sang. By 1984 he had a band built on Fred Smith's guitar and Dug Birdzell's bass, and a sound that took as much from funk and jazz as from hardcore.

years.h: Squip arrives, and drums for Red C
years.p: About nineteen and new to DC from Switzerland, [[Tomas Squip|273702be-180d-487a-9238-2154aea60b92]] plays drums in Red C. He'd go vegetarian within a year or so, a choice that ended up coloring the whole scene.

years.h: Beefeater's line-up: Squip, Smith, Birdzell and Taylor
years.p: Tomas Squip sings, Fred "Freak" Smith plays guitar, Dug E. Bird (Dug Birdzell) plays bass and Bruce Atchley Taylor drums.
years.xp: Fred Smith was a Howard University music-education student whose father sang doo-wop.

years.h: Beefeater's first show: Food for Thought
years.p: Beefeater debut at Food for Thought, the DC restaurant that hosted punk shows. Funk, thrash and reggae in one set, with Tomas Squip's lyrics about politics and spirit.
years.xp:
Dischord's history dates the first show to the summer of 1984 and the band's active run to fall 1984 through fall 1986. The mix was the point: Fred Smith's guitar was aggressive but loose, and Dug Birdzell slapped his bass the way Smith had shown him.

Birdzell has credited Smith with teaching him slap bass. Listeners have heard the [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]] in that combination: punk energy pushed through funk and jazz.

eras.title: Revolution Summer
eras.text: DC hardcore had burned out on violence and the kids who came for it. In 1985 a set of bands tried to make it mean something again, and Beefeater, with its politics and its groove, was one of the pillars.

years.h: Beefeater, one of the Revolution Summer bands
years.p: Beefeater play the season alongside [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]], [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]] and [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]]. Tomas Squip's lyrics are political and openly spiritual, unusual on Dischord.

q: The band that made it all right to talk about vegetarianism.
years.p: Beefeater's debut LP, recorded at Inner Ear and produced by "Gumbo MacKaye." Its song A Dog Day takes the listener into a slaughterhouse.
years.xp:
[[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] was still calling A Dog Day a great song in 2023.

Tomas Squip's vegetarianism wasn't a side note. Soulside's Bobby Sullivan later credited him as the one who got his friends looking at the bigger picture, vegan diet included.

Squip put it simply looking back in 2010: Beefeater gave the scene permission to talk about it.

eras.title: Need a job, then the house burns down
eras.text: Beefeater went through three drummers, put out an EP on another label, and broke up in the fall of 1986 with a finished album nobody had heard yet. Their roadie, Joe Lally, was about to be in Fugazi.

years.h: Bruce Taylor out, Mark Shellhaas in on drums
years.p: Founding drummer Bruce Atchley Taylor leaves Beefeater. Mark Shellhaas plays on the Need a Job EP.

years.h: Need a Job EP · Olive Tree Records
years.p: Six songs on Olive Tree, the only Beefeater record not on Dischord.

years.h: Kenny Craun becomes Beefeater's third drummer
years.p: The third Beefeater drummer in two years. Craun is behind the kit on House Burning Down.

years.h: Beefeater's roadie Joe Lally ends up in Fugazi
years.p: [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]] hauls gear for Beefeater and through the band meets Ian MacKaye, Tomas Squip's roommate. By late summer 1986 Lally is practicing with MacKaye in what becomes [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]].
About two years after the first show, Beefeater is done. House Burning Down, already recorded, is still unreleased.

years.h: Full set at Chevy Chase Community Center, 1986
yt: Full set at Chevy Chase Community Center, 1986

years.p: Out after the breakup. Tomas Squip, Fred Smith, Dug Birdzell and Kenny Craun at Inner Ear, with Ian MacKaye producing again and world music threaded through the funk.

eras.title: Fidelity Jones and Strange Boutique
eras.text: The members scattered into other DC bands, Squip wrote down what he believed for Dischord's own book, and the label put both albums on a single CD.

years.h: Tomas Squip and Dug Birdzell start [[Fidelity Jones|c6332c9e-a2e3-4d2d-8ad7-a6b3ee837717]]
years.p: Squip and Birdzell play in Fidelity Jones until spring 1990. Fred Smith joins the goth-leaning [[Strange Boutique|0ee0668b-fa1d-4db1-ac8c-43a3ad1272c0]], Kenny Craun the Rhythm Pigs.

years.h: Tomas Squip's essay in Threat by Example
years.p: Squip's piece in the Dischord book lays out a plainly religious worldview, rare among Dischord voices. He'd go on to record a solo album, My Happiness, and change his name, first to Onam Ben-Israel and then to Onam Emmet.

years.h: Beefeater's two albums on one CD · Dischord No. 64
years.p: Plays for Lovers and House Burning Down plus bonus tracks, the whole Beefeater Dischord run in one place.

eras.title: Onam and Freak
eras.text: Tomas Squip went looking for God and found several paths. Fred Smith kept playing in bands from post-punk to what he called ghetto metal, took FREAK as his legal name, and was killed in Los Angeles in 2017, a death the DC scene still hasn't had answered.

years.h: Tomas Squip, now Onam Emmet, looks back
years.p: In a 2010 interview, Squip says he spent sixteen years in the African Hebrew Israelite community, a vegan group, before embracing the Sikh path. Washington City Paper had earlier covered his months at the community's commune in Israel.

years.h: Fred Smith's last DC show, at the Black Cat
years.p: Fred Smith's final performance in Washington. By then the Beefeater guitarist had played in Strange Boutique, American Corpse Flower and Blaxmyth.

q: His guitar playing was such a strong element.
years.h: Fred Smith is killed in Los Angeles
years.p: NPR reported that Fred Smith, homeless and in his mid-fifties, was found stabbed to death in Las Palmas Park in San Fernando.
years.xp:
Smith had recently left Blake House, a sober-living facility, and was sleeping on buses and showering at the YMCA, NPR reported.

Ian MacKaye told NPR he'd noticed manic emails and that Smith was dealing with issues of his own. He also called Smith's guitar a huge part of what Beefeater was. Dug Birdzell credited Smith with the band's funk, down to teaching him how to slap.

Police treated the death as a homicide. In December 2017 Los Angeles County offered a $10,000 reward for information, and Supervisor Sheila Kuehl said Smith paved the way for Black musicians in punk. NPR reported that no one had been named.
